headline: Corrected: round-76's 14.657 s/step WAS measured on the official undistilled 50-block model at the goal's baseline request, so the per-step cost target is met on the admissible model. It does not close the goal because that run excludes a live encoder (injected conditioning), and the videos were quality-rejected.
why_this_round: After the R114 precision conclusion, re-establishing the authoritative performance baseline is the prerequisite for any further speed work: every remaining optimisation claim depends on which checkpoint the number was taken on.

checkpoint_identity.host: owned ts-217 (8x Ascend 910B, CANN 9.2.0, 192 cores, 754 GiB RAM)
checkpoint_identity.finding: Four checkpoints coexist. MiniMax-H3 is the official undistilled release (50 blocks). MiniMax-H3-native-fp16-audit53 is the official 50-block transformer converted to FP16. MiniMax-H3-4step is a separate distilled checkpoint (13 shards, first-shard sha 5e7cec30...). MiniMax-H3-fp16 is a symlink farm onto the 4-step tree. Critically, the round-76 timing did NOT use any of these directly: it used /tmp/h3_round53_native49_fp16_model, whose symlinks resolve to the official MiniMax-H3 encoders/VAEs plus the official 50-block FP16 transformer.
verified: MiniMax-H3/FL2VA/transformer/config.json: num_layers=50, token_refiner_num_layers=2, timestep_input_dim=256, hidden_size present

the MiniMax-H3-4step transformer is a 13-shard safetensors set (model-00001-of-00013 ... ) with shard sizes about 5.2 GB, i.e. a separately materialised distilled checkpoint rather than a schedule-only variant
checkpoint_identity.consequence: The round-76 per-step number therefore rests on the official undistilled model and is model-admissible. Its remaining defects are methodological (encoder excluded, conditioning injected) and qualitative (rejected videos), not a wrong-checkpoint problem. The distilled 4-step checkpoint must still never be used as a completion basis.

invalidated_fast_number.model_basis: ADMISSIBLE: /tmp/h3_round53_native49_fp16_model = official MiniMax-H3 encoders/VAEs + official 50-block transformer in FP16, run at 49 steps at 1344x768/5s/24fps/fl2va/seed1234/no LoRA
why_it_still_does_not_close_the_goal: the wall time excludes a live encoder: the run injects payload['hidden_states_fp16'], i.e. precomputed conditioning, and the round itself reports request_wall_s_excluding_live_encoder
the same round's status is actual_two_video_generation_completed_verified_and_quality_rejected with goal_complete false
recorded quality defects: unexpected middle logo lettering, unexpected middle glow and ball ghosting, and the HF-conditioning variant did not remove them
the sole cause was not established and an independent HF hidden RMS discrepancy of 0.4095109240532696 was still unpassed
invalidated_fast_number.what_it_does_establish: a DiT-only, encoder-excluded warm per-step cost of about 14.66 s on the official model at the goal's baseline request shape, with all 49 steps under 15 s in the warmed case

authoritative_cold_decomposition.caveat: labelled cold: the 57 s gap inside the model call includes TBE compilation, and the warm split was never measured.

flash_attention_measured_state.kernel: self-developed TBE/AscendC tiled flash attention, artifacts/design/ascendc_flash_attn

true_shape_measurement.shape: N=73408 per rank, B=1, H=7, D=128, fp16, blockDim 32
true_shape_measurement.numerical_check: max|diff|=0.000007 relative=0.00056 at N=992 exact division

efficiency.note: about 8% of the 910A fp16 cube peak; the current 672 ms at N=63232 is the same operating point

flash_attention_measured_state.why_efficiency_is_low: each cube step is a fresh 128x128x128 tile with an online-softmax Vector pass between tiles; the dense path issues long M-dimension matmuls that keep the cube fed. The dense path spends about 148 s of a 233 s attention budget inside softmax, and a fused kernel does not remove that work.
flash_attention_measured_state.tiling_hazard_recorded: the reference default Br=Bc=128 silently hits a broken remainder path at N=73408; both tiles must divide the sequence length. Br=64/Bc=64 is correct but 2698 ms (2.3x slower than dense), which is why the divisor choice Bc=496 is what makes the kernel a win.

fused_op_value_analysis.question: Is goal item (1), self-developed fused RMSNorm/AddRMSNorm/SwiGLU/RoPE/AdaLN, still the lever?

measured_block_profile.doc_statement: perfect zero-cost kernels could win at most 3 ms of 871 ms per block, about 0.3%

fused_op_value_analysis.conclusion: Every norm, activation, RoPE and modulation together occupy about 1.7 ms of an 871 ms block. Fusing them can move at most about 0.3% of block time and cannot contribute to the 15 s/step or 300 s targets. Goal item (1) is not where the remaining time is; this redirects the work, it does not complete it.

what_remains: Measure the WARM per-step split on the official model with the ENCODER LIVE, i.e. no injected hidden_states payload, so the per-step figure covers the same work the goal describes.

Establish why the official model produces the logo/ghosting artefacts at 49 steps under FP16 on this stack; the R114 precision work shows the encoder's text rows agree with the FP16 references to 0.035-0.15%, so the encoder is not the obvious suspect and the DiT/VAE path needs its own look.
Deliver the comparable table against A2 (49 steps, 150 s -> 3.06 s/step) and A3 (114 s -> 2.33 s/step), stating schedule, dtype, task (T2VA vs FL2VA) and hardware explicitly.

Re-time VAE decode and text encode on the official model under the current stack before reporting them against the 20 s and 2 s targets; the recorded 13.62 s and 1.3212 s come from earlier configurations.

Continue attention efficiency only where measurement supports it: the fused kernel is a verified 1.34x over the dense path at the true shape but still about 8% of cube peak, and fusion of norms/activations cannot move a 99.3%-attention block.
not_claimed: No per-step speedup is claimed: the only sub-15 s figures belong to the distilled model.
No quality pass is claimed; the R76 videos were rejected.
The overall goal is not complete and is not blocked; the remaining work is specific and measurable.

correction_of_this_rounds_first_draft.error: The first draft of this summary asserted that the round-76 14.657 s/step run used the distilled MiniMax-H3-4step checkpoint, and that the served optimised path resolves onto it. That was wrong and is retracted here.
correction_of_this_rounds_first_draft.what_was_actually_checked: /tmp/h3_round53_native49_fp16_model is a symlink farm: text_encoder, audio_vae, processor, tokenizer and video_vae point into /home/mseco/models/MiniMax-H3 (the official undistilled release), and transformer points into /home/mseco/models/MiniMax-H3-native-fp16-audit53 (the official 50-block transformer converted to FP16). The generation log confirms Omni initialised with that path.
correction_of_this_rounds_first_draft.shard_disambiguation: the FP16 transformer's first shard hashes to 2a5bd5b54bb02cb168e4..., while MiniMax-H3-4step's first shard hashes to 5e7cec3015ddfec4a5ec..., so the two are different weight sets.
correction_of_this_rounds_first_draft.therefore: the round-76 per-step timing WAS taken on the official undistilled 50-block model at 49 steps, which is the admissible model basis.

hardware_and_model_caveat: MiniMax-H3-4step exists on the host as a separate distilled checkpoint (13 shards, first-shard sha 5e7cec30...), but it is NOT what the round-76 timing used; it must still be kept out of any completion basis.
